panel-2.notes: Plate 2: debt-service / revenues ratio (%). Pre-computed pipeline-side from DoF Fiscal Monitor multi-year history (FY2019-20 onward). primary=debt_service_ratio (the ratio itself, monthly); secondary=debt_service_ratio_band_lo (5-yr same-month trailing min); tertiary=debt_service_ratio_band_hi (5-yr same-month trailing max). Band methodology: for month m, use the 5 most-recent prior occurrences of the same calendar month (e.g. Feb 2026 band = Feb 2021-2025); requires >=2 prior same-month observations. Source card: plate-2.yaml (Tier A). PBO's 'interest burden' indicator: 10.3c per dollar of revenue currently; rising to 13.2% by 2030-31 (PBO Main Estimates May 2026). PBO endpoint rendered as named anchor in the chart component.

_meta.editorial_context: SUPERSEDES original CAPB spec. The active 2026 fiscal discourse framing is operating-vs-capital under Carney's bifurcated budget, not CAPB. Per Bartlett-Lapointe-Page-Khan methodology brief Q4: 3 of 4 experts do not use CAPB in reader copy.
_meta.headline_narrative: PBO Budget 2025 review identifies a ~$94bn gap (~30%) between DoF's claimed capital investments ($311.5bn over 2024-25 to 2029-30) and PBO's reclassified value ($217.3bn). Reclassified under PBO methodology, the federal operating balance runs deficits in every year of the horizon — even though Budget 2025's headline framing treats much of that spending as 'capital.'

pbo_nov_2025.gap_note: PBO identifies ~$94B gap (~30%) between DoF's 'capital' definition under Budget 2025 ($311.5bn over the horizon) and PBO's stricter definition using IMF GFS 2014 international standard ($217.3bn over the same horizon). The $94B is reclassified from 'capital' to 'operating,' enlarging the operating deficit in every year of the horizon.
